newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: FRENCH SOCIETE GENERALE TO START ACTIVITY.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH SOCIETE GENERALE TO START ACTIVITY.

text.p: French banking giant Societe Generale is to become the first Western bank to start activities in Lithuania, the European Affairs ministry said on Wednesday.
European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene was quoted in a statement during a trip to Paris as saying that she met the heads of the French bank.
"Minister Andrikiene met the heads of Societe Generale. Societe Generale will become the first Western bank to start its activity in our country," Andrikiene was quoted as saying in the statement.
The statement did not say whether this meant that Societe Generale would open a branch or representative office in Lithuania or carry out some other kind of business.
Societe Generale already has a branch office in Latvian capital Riga.
The only foreign bank to have opened a branch office so far in Lithuania is Poland's Kredyt Bank.
Andrikiene could not immediately be contacted to clarify exactly what sort of activity Societe Generale would carry out in Lithuania.
